description: The production portfolio uses Lifecycle V1 for Fastify and Beets: persistent feature-refactor-review workflows with authentic semantic tasks, normal repository discovery, lenient controller-only acceptance, and a strongest-model pilot before treatment spend.

sequences.reset_policy: Each task reset reverses only its generation-local semantic production regression. No acceptance tests are injected. Feature and refactor tasks require affected-component compilation plus one narrow essential-behavior smoke; review tasks remain compile-only. Controller acceptance details are not disclosed as the agent task objective.
sequences.seed_patch_policy: All three generation-local semantic production regressions are applied as one composite start before task 1; prompts remain bounded and final controller verification runs once after the final prompt. Future task regressions remain visible from the start. Model-facing prompts describe the software objective, permit normal repository search and relevant checks, and expect a complete correct implementation; controller acceptance and broader diagnostic treatment are not disclosed.
sequences.conversion_note: Lifecycle V1 replaces the recipe-driven active selector with authentic semantic tasks and normal repository discovery while preserving every executed Baseline V3/V4 contract and result byte-for-byte.
sequences.complexity_note: Lifecycle V1 removes exact edit recipes and target-file restrictions. Agents must inspect the repository, understand the requested behavior, and implement a coherent repair in the persistent workflow. Focused existing-check guidance bounds validation without prescribing edits.
sequences.complexity_bar: Model-facing tasks must state the complete software objective without exposing evaluator scoring. Controller acceptance requires affected-component compilation for every task, one implementation-independent essential-behavior smoke for feature and refactor tasks, and project-wide compilation after the workflow. Review tasks remain compile-only and all broader quality evidence remains diagnostic.

prepared_removals.reason: Six upstream test files fail on a clean checkout of the pinned commit in the sandboxed lane, and not because of anything the pin contains: the sandbox resolves `localhost` to ::1 ahead of 127.0.0.1, so a server bound through a serverFactory listens on ::1 while undici's fetch connects IPv4-first and is refused. Upstream v5.11.3, 34 days past the pin, fails the same seven. Left in place they show the agent seven failures it did not cause and cannot fix, and whether it investigates them is variance charged to the measurement. The controller removes them and commits the removal onto the pinned tree with a fixed identity and date, so the prepared base is a reproducible commit that both the evaluation checkout and the local fixture pin. The clean prepared tree exits zero and every seeded regression still fails underneath.
prepared_removals.commit_message: Fixture preparation: remove tests requiring dual-stack loopback

sequences.conversion_note: Lifecycle V2 replaces three unbounded tasks with a series of comparably sized bounded defect repairs. In V1 the review task carried roughly 45% of session cost and swung 11 steps against 16 on Beets, because 'identify any defect that would be unacceptable to ship' has no terminal condition. Every V2 task restores one named behavior that a specific upstream test already decides, so completion is not a judgement the agent makes about its own thoroughness, and no single task dominates the aggregate.
sequences.complexity_note: Prompts state the observable symptom and never name the file, function, or test involved, so locating the defect remains real retrieval work -- the work the tools under study are meant to make cheaper. Seeds were proven by execution before registration: the seeded state must fail the covering upstream tests and the repaired state must pass them, per scripts/mine_bounded_task_candidates.py.
